findings:
The design is sound and reuses the existing parts well: the space station's laser, hazards, shields, rockets and movers. Four things would go wrong if the tasks ran unattended as planned. First, the test-time budget is added up wrong and leaves out two expensive exit measurements, so the phase would likely hit or pass the 240 s gate limit. Second, the Laser Tender is placed at a moment in Planet Approach that breaks the frozen enemy-density limit. Third, the Deep Space turret group's power source sits right under one of level 1's own laser columns, so the level would kill it and shut the turrets off in every run, and no test would notice. Fourth, many tasks the plan calls parallel edit the same files. The fix: re-plan with a corrected and fully costed time budget, a Tender wave checked against the density gate, a turret placement clear of the columns with a test that checks it, and the shared-file tasks chained one after another. Ten smaller corrections are listed below.

### B1 — gate time
The plan's per-task allotments add up to 26.9 s, not 26.4 s, so the phase ends near 235.3 s rather than 234.8 s, and DECISIONS copies the wrong figure. The drone-pair (t14, 1.0 s) and tender (t19, 5.0 s) tasks must each pay for a new full-corridor curved-exit measurement. One such measurement cost 6.7 s in Phase 7, and the current file with three of them ran 20 s when re-measured. That pushes the gate to about 240 s or over. The plan also lowered the time-saving task's floor from the research's ≥ 15 s to 10 s without explanation.

### B2 — tender density
Using the lives the density gate itself prints, the Laser Tender plus its two drones at planet_approach's 62.0 s wave give 8 counted enemies alive at 65.7 s and 9 at 75.5 s, against the frozen 2.5× ceiling of 7.5. Only the section's opening waves have room.

### B3 — power source under a laser column
`level_1_director.gd:62-68` lights columns at x = 128 / 640 / 1152 at 6.0 s (3 s warning, 4 s active, 9999 damage, hit mask includes enemy hurtboxes). With the camera pinned at (640, 360), `turret_group(...).at(0, -220)` puts the group, and its power source at slot (0, −60), at x = 640. It drifts into the strip exactly while the column is lethal, so every run starts with the group dark. The slice replays drive only `WaveManager`, so no gate would catch this.

### B4 — parallel tasks sharing files
No worktrees are allowed, yet §3 advertises parallel lanes. Pairs with no dependency path between them that edit the same files: t6∥t12 and t11∥t8/t9/t10/t12/t13 (hand `ROSTER`s of the hurtbox and contact-geometry gates, `test_base_enemy.gd`, `test_wreck.gd`, `test_enemy_dual_mode.gd`, `wave_builder.gd`); t7∥t8 (`turret_mount.gd`, `turret_mount_scenes.gd`, `test_defense_turret.gd`); t3∥t5 (`enemy_beam_scenes.gd`); t14∥t16 (tender and drone files and tests); t17∥t19 (`level_1_director.gd`). Chain them, for example t6 → … → t13 → t14 → t16, t3 → t5, t17 → t19.
